description: Inputs at RFC 8785's genuinely divergent edges. We do NOT assert agreement here -- we MAP where independent canonicalizers split, then forbid these shapes from any AlgoVoi preimage at the substrate/schema layer. Proving where the hazard is (not merely avoiding it by luck) is the '100% by design' guarantee.

cases.note: integer just above 2^53: double-based parsers round, arbitrary-precision parsers do not -> hash split. Substrate rule: large counters MUST be string-encoded.
30-digit integer: precision loss varies by runtime.
some impls (strict inline PHP) reject floats; others serialize. Substrate rule: no floats in preimages.
0.1 has no exact double; formatting of the shortest round-trip can differ.
negative zero: -0 vs 0 handling differs (ECMAScript prints 0).
exponent form: normalized to 1000 by some, preserved by others.
overflows IEEE754 double to Infinity in most runtimes -> reject or divergence.
NaN is not valid JSON; lenient parsers (Python) accept it -> split vs strict parsers.
Infinity is not valid JSON; lenient parsers accept -> split.
duplicate keys: last-wins vs error varies by parser. Substrate rule: reject duplicate keys before hashing.
decomposed e+combining-acute vs precomposed é: JCS does NOT normalize, so visually equal strings hash differently. Substrate rule: NFC-normalize identifiers before binding.
lone high surrogate: some encoders emit replacement char, some error.

leading zero is invalid JSON per RFC 8259, but Go/Java/.NET canonicalizers ACCEPT and normalize it while Python/Node/Ruby/Rust/PHP reject -> real accept/reject split. Substrate rule: reject leading-zero numbers before hashing.
